solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Crane carrying copper hours before silver in a stone box (11)

indicators.note: the crane holds the next pieces inside it
hours comes ahead of silver in the run of letters
the stuffing sits inside the crane

blocks.note: the sarus is an Asian crane; it opens round the rest
copper = policeman = COP
h = hours
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: A crane on a building site lifts a policeman, then some silver, into a stone coffin.
annotation.walkthrough: Copper is not Cu here but a police officer. The sarus crane is the one bird crosswords lean on for SARUS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the ancient Egyptians and Romans buried their dead in carved stone coffins of this name.

entries.clue: Bag search regularly omitted (3)

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped, leaving S, A, C

blocks.note: S(e)A(r)C(h): first, third and fifth letters

annotation.surface: A bag search at an airport is being skipped as a matter of routine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' in a clue almost always means alternate letters, and 'omitted' tells you the even ones go.
annotation.definitionFit: A sac is a bag-like pouch, as in a plant or animal.

entries.clue: Media person out of place for 1215 signing far from set (5)

indicators.note: the Media person is taken out of the place name

blocks.note: Magna Carta was sealed at Runnymede in 1215
a Mede was a native of Media, an ancient kingdom in Iran; removed

annotation.surface: A journalist is stuck somewhere, far from the film set, at the anniversary of an old treaty signing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Media person' looks like a journalist; it is a Mede, from the ancient land of Media. RUNNYMEDE is the meadow by the Thames where King John agreed Magna Carta.
annotation.definitionFit: A jelly or egg that is far from set is still runny.

entries.clue: Unacceptable move here in consequence (7)

blocks.note: out = not allowed, as in 'that's out'
to come is to move towards the speaker

annotation.surface: Making a forbidden move has consequences.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Move here' reads like a chess instruction but is simply COME.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean the result that follows from an action.

entries.clue: Moment that a beer is drunk (9)

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone notes how quickly a beer gets downed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' is doubly apt: it fits the beer in the surface and is a standard anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: In a heartbeat means in a moment; a heartbeat is a very short time.

entries.clue: Spirit that can be released by rubber (5)

definitions.text: Spirit that can be released by rubber

blocks.note: reads as alcohol escaping, but the spirit is a supernatural being set free
reads as a rubber seal or bung, but the rubber is a person rubbing an old lamp, as in the Aladdin story

annotation.surface: Alcohol that escapes from a rubber seal or bung.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' tempts towards drink and 'rubber' towards a material; the rubber is a person who rubs a lamp.
annotation.definitionFit: A genie is a spirit freed by rubbing the lamp that holds it.

entries.clue: Slight errors ultimately by building society? (7)

indicators.note: take the last letter of errors

blocks.note: last letter of errorS
a building society lends mortgages; the ? marks it as one example

annotation.surface: A building society has made a few small mistakes.
annotation.walkthrough: A building society is a British mutual bank that lends for house purchase, so it is a LENDER.
annotation.definitionFit: Slight and slender both mean thin or small.

entries.clue: Shoot and what to root it in (3)

blocks.note: the verb: to shoot game, or sink a snooker ball
a flowerpot, to root a cutting in

annotation.surface: A gardener takes a cutting and asks what to plant it in.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Shoot' a plant stem; as a definition it is the verb, to fire at.
annotation.definitionFit: Pot means shoot (a pot shot), and a pot is where a cutting takes root.

entries.clue: Feline’s caught in joint up one old tree (9)

indicators.note: the feline's letters sit inside the joint
in a down clue, up reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: the hip joint, opened round the cat
cat's, with the apostrophe s kept; H(CATS)IP reads upwards as PISTACH
I = one
o = old

annotation.surface: A cat has got stuck in a joint while climbing an old tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The feline's 's is not grammar: it supplies the S of PISTACHIO.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by kind: the green nut we eat grows on a small tree of the same name.

entries.clue: Betraying monarch elates baron terribly (11)

indicators.note: the letters are treated terribly, knocked out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A king betrays his subjects, much to a baron's delight.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase, 'betraying the monarch', which is what treason is.
annotation.definitionFit: Treasonable acts betray the monarch or state.

entries.clue: Check constant wet weather (9)

blocks.note: const is the usual abbreviation of constant
rain = wet weather

annotation.surface: A forecaster checks the unending wet weather.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check' is a verb here, to hold back, not a look at something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to check something is to hold it back or restrict it.

entries.clue: Succeed? Make certain king has departed (5)

indicators.note: the king has left the word

blocks.note: ensure = make certain
R = rex, king; removed

annotation.surface: An heir asks whether they will succeed, having made sure the king is gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' suggests taking the throne; here it means follow on, which is what ensue does.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the older sense of succeed: to come next, follow on after.

entries.clue: Steer clear of my bed, as some might say (7)

definitions.text: my bed, as some might say

blocks.note: to avoid on principle, refusing to deal with

blocks.clueFragment: my bed, as some might say
blocks.note: a small boy might call his bed his BOY COT

annotation.surface: Someone tells another person to keep off their bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: 'some' who might say 'my bed' are boys, and a boy's bed is a cot.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is a protest refusal to deal with someone; the second is a nursery joke, a boy's cot being his bed.

entries.clue: What can follow eggs in eastern liqueur? (11)

blocks.note: eggs Benedict, the brunch dish
used as itself
E = eastern

annotation.surface: Someone asks what might come after eggs soaked in an oriental liqueur.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the wordplay, supplying IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a French herbal liqueur named after the monks said to have first made it.

entries.clue: Upright, having finish and manners (7)

blocks.note: end = finish
ways = manners, habits

annotation.surface: An upright person with polish and good manners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upright' reads as honest; the definition is the physical sense, standing on end.
annotation.definitionFit: A physical synonym: standing on its end means standing upright.

entries.clue: Fine about European mum’s name for my cousin? (5)

indicators.note: fine goes round the European

blocks.note: nice = fine, pleasant; opened round E
E = European

annotation.surface: A European mother says a lovely word about a family member.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a family puzzle: my cousin is my mother's niece, so that is what mum would call her.
annotation.definitionFit: Your cousin, if a girl, is your mother's niece.

entries.clue: Run minutes into level match when winners may be decided (5,4)

indicators.note: 'into' places the minutes inside the level match, so the tie is split open to hold M

blocks.note: in cricket a run not scored off the bat is an extra
a tie is a drawn game; opened round M
m = minutes

annotation.surface: A drawn match runs on for some minutes while the winners are decided.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run the batter did not hit, such as a wide or a bye, so 'Run' can give EXTRA.
annotation.definitionFit: Extra time is played after a drawn match so a winner may emerge.

entries.clue: Dying to get hard professional backing with popular pain blocker (9)

indicators.note: hard and professional are read backwards together

blocks.note: one's end is one's dying
h = hard, as on pencils
pro = professional
in = fashionable, popular

annotation.surface: A dying patient, backed by a well-liked doctor, wants a painkiller.
annotation.walkthrough: Hard and professional make HPRO, which read backwards is ORPH.
annotation.definitionFit: Endorphins are the body's own chemicals that block pain.

entries.clue: Instruction from dreadful court — a number beheaded (9)

indicators.note: the number loses its first letter

blocks.note: dire = dreadful
ct is the abbreviation of court
(F)IVE with its head off

annotation.surface: An order comes from a terrible court, with one of its members executed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A number' is deliberately vague; any number might do until the crossers point to FIVE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for an order issued by an authority.

entries.clue: What might cause boom to trade on bananas (9)

indicators.note: bananas = crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: An economist asks what could start a boom in the banana trade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boom' looks economic, and 'bananas' looks like the traded goods; the boom is an explosion.
annotation.definitionFit: A detonator sets off an explosive, causing the boom.

entries.clue: Bliss of Hindus, those at the front welcomed by circulating rani (7)

indicators.note: the front group goes inside the rani
the rani's letters rotate, RANI becoming NIRA

blocks.note: a rani is an Indian queen; RANI rotated to NIRA, opened round VAN
the van is the front of an army

annotation.surface: A travelling Indian queen greets her leading followers in a moment of Hindu bliss.
annotation.walkthrough: A rani is the wife of a rajah, an Indian queen. 'Those at the front' means the vanguard, the leading troops.
annotation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist thought nirvana is the state of perfect bliss.

entries.clue: Ring found during search in hollow (5)

indicators.note: the ring sits in the middle of the search

blocks.note: to comb an area is to search it; opened round O
O is ring-shaped

annotation.surface: A lost ring turns up while searching in a dip in the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: A coomb (or combe) is a short valley in southern England; the word is rare outside crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: in southern England a short valley or hollow in a hillside.

entries.clue: Long period interrupted by concerning depression (7)

indicators.note: the long period is broken open by the next word

blocks.note: a cycle is a long period, an era; opened round ON
on = about, concerning

annotation.surface: A long spell of low mood is broken by a new worry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' is the weather sense, an area of low pressure, not low mood.
annotation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a low-pressure system, a meteorological depression.

entries.clue: Embarrassed after fish is burnt (7)

indicators.note: embarrassed comes after the fish

blocks.note: char is a trout-like fish
red-faced = embarrassed

annotation.surface: A cook is red-faced after burning the fish.
annotation.walkthrough: Char the fish and char the verb share a spelling, which the surface exploits.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scorched black on the surface by fire.

entries.clue: Abandon desire to follow Democrat (5)

indicators.note: desire comes after the Democrat

blocks.note: D = Democrat
an itch is a craving

annotation.surface: A voter gives up the urge to back the Democrats.
annotation.walkthrough: D for Democrat comes from US politics, where it tags a politician's party.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: to drop or get rid of something, as you might ditch a plan or a partner.

entries.clue: A feather in one’s cap? Nonsense, a hollow debacle (7)

indicators.note: the debacle is emptied, leaving only its ends

blocks.note: cock = nonsense, as in 'a load of cock'
used as itself
outer letters of D(ebacl)E, the middle hollowed out

annotation.surface: Someone dismisses a supposed triumph as an empty fiasco.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition takes the idiom literally: a cockade is a rosette or knot worn on a hat, so it really is in one's cap.
annotation.definitionFit: A cockade is a ribbon or rosette decoration worn on a hat.

entries.clue: Out of the way location for resort, not the southeast (5)

indicators.note: the southeast is taken away

blocks.note: a resort is usually at the seaside
SE = southeast; removed

annotation.surface: Someone wants a remote resort, anywhere but the south-east of England.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the first SE of SEASIDE is removed, leaving ASIDE.
annotation.definitionFit: Aside means out of the way, as in 'step aside'.

entries.clue: Island of India with casual business area (5)

blocks.note: India is I in the NATO alphabet
biz is informal for business
a = area

annotation.surface: An Indian island with a relaxed commercial district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Casual' marks the slang form, BIZ rather than BUSINESS.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

entries.clue: Making gear to track seal (9)

blocks.note: to tail someone is to track them
an O-ring is a rubber seal

annotation.surface: Assembling equipment to follow a seal across the ice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gear' suggests machinery but means clothes; 'seal' is not the animal but a gasket.
annotation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothes, and cutting and sewing clothes to measure is the tailor's trade.

entries.clue: Powerful boat goes up narrow channel (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue the boat is read upwards

blocks.note: a tug is a small powerful boat; read upwards

annotation.surface: A tug heads up a narrow waterway.
annotation.walkthrough: A gut is a narrow strait or channel of water, a sense seldom met outside crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: a narrow strait or water passage, by analogy with the intestine.

entries.clue: Girl at no time stripped (3)

indicators.note: the word is stripped of its outer letters

blocks.note: never = at no time; stripped of its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A girl who never undressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At no time' is NEVER; strip it and the middle is a girl's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'girl' in crosswords often stands for any female first name, here the first woman in Genesis.

entries.clue: Heraldic display of a feather in one’s cap (11)

blocks.note: the technical heraldic term for a full coat of arms
a feather in one's cap is an accomplishment

annotation.surface: A coat of arms shows a feather worn in a hat.
annotation.walkthrough: The heraldic sense is the technical one: shield, crest, supporters and motto together make the achievement.
annotation.definitionFit: An achievement is both a full heraldic coat of arms and an accomplishment.
